topic: COLUMNS(* REPLACE ...) and paren-less * REPLACE / EXCLUDE / RENAME star modifiers

pins.q: SELECT COLUMNS(* REPLACE (a + 10 AS a, b + 20 AS b)) FROM test_t1 NATURAL JOIN test_t2
pins.note: Corpus verbatim. NATURAL JOIN order: join column a first, then t1 leftover b, then t2 leftover c. REPLACE keeps names/positions, only values change.

pins.q: SELECT COLUMNS(* REPLACE (concat(a::VARCHAR, '_joined') AS a)) FROM test_t1 NATURAL JOIN test_t2
pins.note: Corpus verbatim. Replaced column changes type (INTEGER->VARCHAR) but keeps name and position.

pins.q: SELECT COLUMNS(* REPLACE (a + 10 AS a)) FROM test_t1
pins.note: Single table: identical to plain * REPLACE.

pins.q: SELECT COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE b) FROM test_t1
pins.note: Paren-less EXCLUDE inside COLUMNS also legal, same result.

pins.q: SELECT COLUMNS(*) FROM test_t1 NATURAL JOIN test_t2
pins.note: Re-verified: same NATURAL JOIN order as plain *.

pins.q: SELECT abs(COLUMNS(* REPLACE (a + 10 AS a))) FROM test_t1
pins.note: Wrapper naming: REPLACEd column gets full rendered expression text with ':=' syntax; NON-replaced column keeps bare name 'b' (no 'abs(b)'). Baseline SELECT abs(COLUMNS(*)) FROM test_t1 gives names=['a','b'] rows=[(1,2)] — bare-column inputs always keep bare names.

pins.q: SELECT COLUMNS(* REPLACE (z + 1 AS z)) FROM test_t1
pins.result: BinderException: Binder Error: Column "z" in REPLACE list not found in FROM clause
pins.note: Nonexistent REPLACE target is a binder error, exact text pinned.

pins.q: SELECT COLUMNS('a|b' REPLACE (a + 10 AS a)) FROM test_t1
pins.result:
ParserException: Parser Error: syntax error at or near "REPLACE"

LINE 1: SELECT COLUMNS('a|b' REPLACE (a + 10 AS a)) FROM test_t1
                             ^
pins.note: COLUMNS('regex' REPLACE ...) combined form is ILLEGAL — parser error. Same for COLUMNS('a' REPLACE ...). Star modifiers only attach to * inside COLUMNS.

pins.q: SELECT * REPLACE i+100 AS i FROM integers
pins.note: Corpus verbatim. Paren-less single REPLACE = parenthesized single REPLACE.

pins.q: SELECT * REPLACE i+100 AS i, j+1 AS j FROM integers
pins.note: LEGAL but the comma ENDS the star item. Paren-less REPLACE consumes exactly ONE replacement; ', j+1 AS j' becomes a second SELECT-list item -> 3 columns with duplicate name 'j'. NOT equivalent to two replacements.

pins.q: SELECT * REPLACE (i+100 AS i, j+1 AS j) FROM integers
pins.note: Contrast: parenthesized form is the only way to get multiple replacements.

pins.q: SELECT * EXCLUDE i, j FROM integers
pins.note: Comma ends the star item: * EXCLUDE i (-> j) plus a separate projection of j. Duplicate output names allowed.

pins.q: SELECT * RENAME i AS q FROM integers
pins.note: Paren-less RENAME works. Two-item paren-less variant SELECT * RENAME i AS q, j AS r FROM integers gives names=['q','j','r'] rows=[(1,2,2)] — same comma-splits-into-new-item rule.

pins.q: SELECT integers.* REPLACE i+100 AS i FROM integers
pins.note: Paren-less modifier legal after a qualified star too.

pins.q: SELECT * REPLACE i+100 AS i LIKE 'i%' FROM integers
pins.result:
BinderException: Binder Error: Replace list cannot be combined with a filtering operation

LINE 1: SELECT * REPLACE i+100 AS i LIKE 'i%' FROM integers
                                    ^
pins.note: PARSES fine (LIKE after paren-less REPLACE is grammatically accepted) but binder rejects the combination. Identical error without FROM. Baseline SELECT * LIKE 'i%' FROM integers works alone: names=['i'] rows=[(1,)]. Reverse order SELECT * LIKE 'i%' REPLACE (i+100 AS i) FROM integers is a ParserException at REPLACE.

pins.result: BinderException: Binder Error: SELECT list is empty after resolving * expressions!
pins.note: Excluding every column is a binder error, exact text pinned.

surprises: Two-item paren-less REPLACE is LEGAL but does NOT mean two replacements: the comma terminates the star item and starts a new SELECT-list item, producing extra duplicate-named columns (names ['i','j','j']). Same for EXCLUDE i, j (-> ['j','j']) and RENAME two items (-> ['q','j','r']). A compiler that parses paren-less lists greedily across commas would be wrong.
COLUMNS('regex' REPLACE ...) is a ParserException — REPLACE/EXCLUDE only combine with * (or qualified star), never with the regex form of COLUMNS.

abs(COLUMNS(* REPLACE ...)) names asymmetrically: the replaced column becomes 'abs(a := (a + 10))' (note the ':=' rendering of the replace item), while non-replaced columns keep their bare names ('b', not 'abs(b)').

Star filter + REPLACE incompatibility is a BINDER error ('Replace list cannot be combined with a filtering operation'), not a parser error — 'SELECT * REPLACE i+100 AS i LIKE ...' parses; and the binder raises this even with no FROM clause. LIKE-before-REPLACE is the parser error.
summary: DuckDB 1.5.5. COLUMNS(* REPLACE ...) and plain * REPLACE are name/position-preserving: output keeps original column names and star expansion order (NATURAL JOIN order = join columns first, then left-table leftovers, then right-table leftovers), with only the replaced column's value/type changing. EXCLUDE inside COLUMNS works both parenthesized and paren-less; COLUMNS('regex' REPLACE ...) is a parser error — modifiers attach only to the star form. When COLUMNS(* REPLACE ...) is wrapped in a function like abs(), only the replaced column gets a rendered-expression name ('abs(a := (a + 10))'); untouched columns keep bare names. Critical grammar rule: paren-less REPLACE/EXCLUDE/RENAME consume exactly ONE item — a following comma starts a new independent SELECT-list item (yielding duplicate output names), so multi-item modifiers require parentheses; paren-less modifiers also work after qualified stars (t.*). REPLACE cannot combine with a star filter: 'LIKE after REPLACE' parses but binder-errors ('Replace list cannot be combined with a filtering operation'), 'REPLACE after LIKE' is a parser error. Error pins: unknown REPLACE target -> Binder Error: Column \"z\" in REPLACE list not found in FROM clause; excluding all columns -> Binder Error: SELECT list is empty after resolving * expressions!
